holidays.name: National Bagel and Lox Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the classic deli combo of a chewy bagel, silky smoked salmon, cream cheese, and a few tasty extras. Common extras are capers, red onion, and tomato. Brunch fans, this one is for you.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its creator is unclear. It became popular through food-holiday calendars, which pair it with the long tradition of Jewish-American delis.
holidays.funFact: Bagels and lox became a New York deli staple in the early 20th century. Cream cheese joined the pairing as dairy and fish-curing traditions mixed in Jewish immigrant communities.

holidays.name: National Toothache Day
holidays.description: This day is an awareness day about the nagging, throbbing misery of a sore tooth. It nudges you to brush, floss, and book that dental checkup you keep dodging.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is used as an annual reminder about oral health and not putting off dental care.
holidays.funFact: The word "toothache" is so old that people have written about remedies for it for thousands of years. Ancient texts describe treatments such as herbal poultices and even prayers.

holidays.name: National Pizza Day
holidays.description: Cheese pulls, crispy crusts, and pepperoni cups for everyone. Pizza fans mark the day with a slice, a whole pie, or a daring pineapple debate.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance whose exact creator is unclear. Pizza chains and food fans now promote it every year with deals and social media posts.
holidays.funFact: Pizza is said to have been born in Naples, Italy. The classic Margherita is often credited as a nod to Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889.
